inspector.heading: Context Inspector
inspector.description: Inspect one compilation's context structure. The view renders exactly what the Core serves about the compilation — the selected and omitted sources with their Core-provided reasons, the budget facts, and the exactness label. The context preview is an inspection view, never canonical knowledge truth.
inspector.loading: Reading the context snapshot from the Core…
inspector.noJob: Name the compilation job whose context to inspect, then select Inspect. Job context links on the job detail surface open this view directly.
inspector.gateNoteBody: Save snapshot and snapshot compare stay hidden while their recorded preconditions stand: durable snapshot storage and stable Core comparison do not exist yet (both decisions are recorded as the owner's pending decisions). Nothing is saved, compared, or fabricated while the preconditions stand.
inspector.nonCanonicalNote: This inspection view is NOT canonical knowledge truth. It shows what influenced a compilation; it never implies the model produces the same output every time.
inspector.reconstructionNote: Reproducibility means the exact source references, the rendered request version, the tool outputs, and the policy versions can be reconstructed — it is never a model-output determinism guarantee.
inspector.sensitivityNote: The compilation reveals what influenced a result — this view is sensitive. Sources are shown as references, digests, and reasons; content is never rendered wholesale.
inspector.failureBody: The Core refused the context snapshot read. The refusal below is shown exactly as the Core returned it.
inspector.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.
inspector.unknownTitle: The context read did not confirm
inspector.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A timeout is never treated as an outcome. Refresh to re-query the authoritative read.
inspector.notFoundTitle: No context snapshot for this job
inspector.notFoundBody: The Core reports no stored context snapshot for this job reference. The typed refusal is shown exactly as the Core returned it.

view.exactCoreProducedNote: The Core reports this snapshot as its own stored immutable record. Even the exact state never implies deterministic model output.
view.approximateNote: The compiler could not reproduce the exact rendered context. The available provenance is shown instead of an exact claim; the label comes only from the Core-reported state.
view.includedEmpty: The Core reports no included sources for this snapshot.
view.omittedEmpty: The Core reports no omitted sources — no silent truncation is recorded for this compilation.
view.reasonUnavailableNote: The Core reports this omission without a reason. The absence is displayed as the absence — the UI never invents why a source was chosen or omitted.
view.estimateNote: The Core's compiled estimate, labeled by its estimator version ({{estimator}}).
view.usedNote: The provider/Core usage-reporting fields are not supplied yet (the owner's pending decision). Actual usage renders only when the provider reports it — never an extrapolated or computed value.
view.metadataNote: The published metadata extension (workflow/run references, source digest classes, used budget, model target, snapshot digest, representation version) has no serving source today — no standalone compiled-context read exists. Unavailable fields render as Unavailable and are never invented.

inclusion.title: Set the per-request memory inclusion
inclusion.description: An explicit decision about which memory items are included in the stated request's compiled context. The decision applies ONLY to the stated request reference — it changes no memory item's state, creates no memory action row, and never widens any scope.
inclusion.requestRefHint: The ONLY scope this decision applies to. Retention is request-lifetime at most.
inclusion.correlationHint: Identifies this decision for the same-request replay (the reconcile path for a lost response).
inclusion.confirmedTitle: The Core confirmed the decision record
inclusion.confirmedBody: The decision applies to the stated request only. The Core-confirmed outcomes render below; a reason renders only where the Core reports one.
inclusion.failureBody: The Core refused the inclusion decision. The refusal below is shown exactly as the Core returned it.
inclusion.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A timeout is never treated as an outcome. Re-issue the SAME decision (the same request reference and correlation ID) — the Core's same-request replay is the reconcile path, never a blind repeat.

operations.heading: Operation status
operations.description: Read one context operation's authoritative state by its operation ID. This read is the reconcile path for a lost response — a timeout is never treated as success, failure, or safe retry.
operations.failureBody: The Core refused the operation-state read. The refusal below is shown exactly as the Core returned it.
operations.unknownTitle: The operation read did not confirm
operations.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A timeout is never treated as an outcome. Re-query the authoritative read.
operations.notFoundBody: The Core reports no such context operation. The unknown and out-of-scope identities are the same typed refusal — the UI never infers existence from a refusal.

failure.CONTEXT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: The context budget was exhausted — the explicit omission record is the outcome, never a silent truncation. A repeat with the same budget re-exhausts it.
failure.CONTEXT_OMISSION_REASON_UNAVAILABLE: The Core reports an omission without a reason. The absence is displayed as the absence — no reason is synthesized. The read may be re-issued safely.
failure.CONTEXT_COMPILATION_UNAVAILABLE: The compilation or preview cannot be served right now. The unavailable state renders honestly — never a fabricated state. The read may be re-issued safely.
failure.CONTEXT_COMPARE_UNSUPPORTED: Snapshot compare is not supported yet: stable Core comparison does not exist. The comparison-unavailable state renders honestly and no diff is fabricated. The read-only re-issue is safe while the outcome persists.
failure.CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND: No such context snapshot or operation. The unknown and out-of-scope identities carry the same typed refusal.
failure.CONFLICT_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: The idempotency key was already used with a different request identity. Use a fresh key for a new request.
failure.CONFLICT_STATE: The recorded state conflicts with the request (for example, a replay past its window). Reconcile through the authoritative state read before any retry.
failure.MEMORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND: No such memory item. The unknown and out-of-scope identities carry the same typed refusal.
failure.AUTHZ_DENIED: The Core refused the authorization decision for this effect.
failure.INTERNAL: An internal Core error. The correlation ID identifies the refusal in the Core's records.
failure.unlisted: The Core returned a refusal code outside the known register. It is shown verbatim, never mapped.

recovery.CONTEXT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: Review the omission record; adjust the request before repeating.
recovery.CONTEXT_OMISSION_REASON_UNAVAILABLE: Refresh to re-query the authoritative read.
recovery.CONTEXT_COMPILATION_UNAVAILABLE: Refresh to re-query; the state may resolve on its own.
recovery.CONTEXT_COMPARE_UNSUPPORTED: Wait for the recorded precondition to resolve; the re-issue is safe but will answer the same refusal until then.
recovery.CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND: Check the identifier; the read is safe to re-issue.
recovery.CONFLICT_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: Reconcile through the authoritative state read; use a fresh key for a genuinely new request.
recovery.CONFLICT_STATE: Reconcile through the authoritative state read before any retry.
recovery.MEMORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND: Check the memory item ID on the Memory surface.
recovery.NOT_FOUND: Check the identifier; the read is safe to re-issue.
recovery.AUTHZ_DENIED: The effect requires an authorized session.
recovery.INTERNAL: Retry once after a pause; if it persists, report the correlation ID.
recovery.unlisted: Treat the refusal as final; reconcile through the authoritative read before any retry.
